title: Avoid multiple SQL function compilations when preparing a parallel filter/GROUP BY query
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, when compiling a parallel filter/GROUP BY query we're compiling SQL functions from AST multiple times, once per the owner query thread and each shared worker thread. We could speed up the query compilation by compiling the functions only once and then cloning the functions per worker. This needs a new `deepClone()` method on the `Function` interface and proper implementations in all functions.

### Describe the solution you'd like.

comments.body: The problem is that a `GroupByFunction` may wrap a number of non-group by functions as its arguments and, when a `deepClone()` happens, it needs to clone them as well. So, due to that all `Function`s have to support `deepClone()`.

In my humble option,  non-group by functions seems have no inner-state, which mean is thread-safe access, may  the `GroupByFunction`'s  non-group by functions arg need not Deepclone ? (Shared between different `GroupByFunction` objects by reference/pointer)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Many non-group by functions have runtime state which makes them non-thread safe. E.g. if the query has `first(concat(str_col, 'foobar'))` as an aggregate, the `ConcatFunction` function will have a `StringSink` to accumulate the concatenated strings.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Many non-group by functions have runtime state which makes them non-thread safe. E.g. if the query has `first(concat(str_col, 'foobar'))` as an aggregate, the `ConcatFunction` function will have a `StringSink` to accumulate the concatenated strings.

OK，I checked  the `StrFunction` and most of are not thread-safe to reuse alloc memory.
So here `deepCloneIfNeed` can implement as:
- if `isThreadSafe` return true, return `this` as pointer;
- if `isThreadSafe` return false, only clone necessary fields that not thread-safe
- if `isThreadSafe` depend on its warper child function, clone itself and then call its warper function recursive

Is it ok to implement by this way?
Can i work on this issue?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Is it ok to implement by this way?
> Can i work on this issue?

I'd prefer cloning the functions unconditionally since this is less error-prone: it matches the current behavior when we recompile each function. As for working on the issue, sure please go ahead!

comments.body: ATM `CursorFunction` can be used only in `IN (<symbol sub-query>)` and `IN (<timestamp sub-query>)` expressions in WHERE clause. So, it doesn't need implementing `deepClone()`, but instead can throw an exception.
